unverified: No claim failed the check; everything below is unverified by design, not by check result.

Ousmane's first recordings: Jones (2024) says Ousmane were the first group to record popular music in Tamazight, French Wikipedia says Izenzaren's first cassette was in 1974. Not resolved; began is set to 1972 (Izenzaren's formation), with no 'attested'.
Origin coordinates (Dcheira, 30.37, -9.53) are approximate, not from a source.
Peak window 1975-1995 is a judgement from dated facts (tazenzart dominant from 1975, Archach 1979, Oudaden 1978 and first album 1985), not stated by any source.
Oudaden album count disagrees: English Wikipedia 'thirty-eight albums', French Wikipedia 'une trentaine', and Le Matin (cited there) '28e album' in 2012; the Le Matin page was not read.
Oudaden's Mayna: French Wikipedia says 2012, iTunes release date 2013-01-01 with a 2022 copyright line; year left null.
Amarg Fusion has no song: no catalogue page found for its albums Agadir Ifawne (2006) and Argan d'Oufgan (Yabiladi names both; last.fm refused the script).
Khalid Izri and the Rif (Tarifit) bands such as Tawattun are left out of scope; see notes.
Africangrooves calls Ousmane 'Amazighe (berber tribe from North Africa) Gnawa music': not used, contradicted by the scholarly articles.
